# dsortr

> Sorts the values in `x1` with a gapped (Shell) insertion sort, optionally applying the same permutation to a companion vector `x2`.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dsortr from '@rreusser/blahpack/arpack/dsortr';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dsortr( which, apply, N, x1, strideX1, x2, strideX2 ) → Float64Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `which` | `"LM" \| "SM" \| "LA" \| "SA"` | Ordering: `'LM'`, `'SM'`, `'LA'`, or `'SA'` |
| `apply` | `boolean` | Whether to apply the sorting permutation to `x2` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elements to sort |
| `x1` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 0:N-1</sub> | **in/out** · Array whose values determine (and receive) the sort |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | Stride length for `x1` |
| `x2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 0:N-1</sub> | **in/out** · Companion array permuted alongside `x1` when `apply` is `true` |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | Stride length for `x2` |

**Returns** `Float64Array`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "LM", "SM", "LA", "SA"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Strided (strided) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dsortr.strided(
    which,
    apply,
    N,
    x1, strideX1, offsetX1,
    x2, strideX2, offsetX2
) → Float64Array
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `which` | `"LM" \| "SM" \| "LA" \| "SA"` | Ordering: `'LM'`, `'SM'`, `'LA'`, or `'SA'` |
| `apply` | `boolean` | Whether to apply the sorting permutation to `x2` |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Number of elements to sort |
| `x1` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 0:N-1</sub> | **in/out** · Array whose values determine (and receive) the sort |
| ↳ `strideX1` | `integer` | Stride length for `x1` |
| ↳ `offsetX1` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `x1` |
| `x2` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length 0:N-1</sub> | **in/out** · Companion array permuted alongside `x1` when `apply` is `true` |
| ↳ `strideX2` | `integer` | Stride length for `x2` |
| ↳ `offsetX2` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `x2` |

**Returns** `Float64Array`

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "LM", "SM", "LA", "SA"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dsortr from './../lib/base.js';

// Ritz values and a companion vector (e.g. their error bounds):
const x1 = new Float64Array( [ 3.0, -1.0, 4.0, -1.5, 2.0 ] );
const x2 = new Float64Array( [ 10.0, 20.0, 30.0, 40.0, 50.0 ] );

// Sort so the largest algebraic value ends up last, permuting x2 alongside:
dsortr( 'LA', true, 5, x1, 1, 0, x2, 1, 0 );

console.log( x1 ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => <Float64Array>[ -1.5, -1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0 ]

console.log( x2 ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
// => <Float64Array>[ 40.0, 20.0, 50.0, 10.0, 30.0 ]
```

</section>
